Make the problem smaller
The mind likes to turn quitting into an enormous promise.
9:41
Close
Never again.
Ninety days.
The rest of your life.
9:41
Close
At midnight, those promises are almost useless. They ask a tired version of you to carry a future that has not happened yet.
So do not carry it.
9:41
Close
Get to tomorrow.
9:41
Close
What tonight requires
For the next few hours, the job is simple: do not relapse.
9:41
Close
Not forever.
Not for the next three months.
Not even for the rest of the week.
Just tonight.
9:41
Close
Tomorrow, we can work on the habit itself.
Tonight, make sure it does not get another round.
9:41
Close
Think about the last night
Go back to the last time it happened at night. Where were you before the searching started?
9:41
Close
Maybe you were in bed with your phone. Maybe you could not sleep. Maybe you had a bad day and wanted something that would switch your head off for a while.
9:41
Close
There is usually an earlier moment when stopping is cheap.
Before the search.
Before the tab.
Before you are fully caught in it.
9:41
Close
Where do most of your night-time relapses begin?
Pick the one that happens most.
In bed with my phone
Alone on my computer
When I can’t sleep
Somewhere else
Continue
9:41
Close
Add distance
An urge at midnight is much more convincing when the whole habit sits one thumb-movement away.
Change that.
9:41
Close
If the phone is across the room, you have to stand up. If it is downstairs, you have to leave the bed.
9:41
Close
If the laptop is closed and put away, you have to make another decision before anything happens.
That small gap matters. Do not spend willpower where distance will do the job.
9:41
Close
Before you sleep

No huge promise about the future.
No test of whether you are “strong enough.”

Tomorrow can have tomorrow.

84I2 · D01 — Task 2 of 2

Match where you sleep
Own bedroom
Set the alarm now. Charge the phone outside the room. Put a laptop or tablet in a closed bag, drawer, or cupboard away from the bed.
Shared room
Put the device in a bag, locker, desk drawer, or fixed charging spot that you cannot reach while lying down.
Studio, sofa bed, or temporary space
Put the device at the farthest practical point from where you sleep: a kitchen counter, shelf, zipped bag, or other fixed place.
Phone needed as an alarm
Set the alarm first. Put the phone across the room or outside it. Turn off non-essential notifications before you put it down.
Mark as done
